issues.description: IAM-policy fetch failure silently classifies image as not publicly shared, weakening the PASS postcondition.
issues.detail: In _get_images, when getIamPolicy raises (e.g., permission denied on fixture image 3), the except branch logs and leaves publicly_shared=False, so the check reports PASS for an unverified image. PASS should mean 'verified non-public', not 'we could not tell'. Introduce a tri-state (unknown/MANUAL) or surface an error finding so the contract is honest.

issues.description: Check name is inconsistent between PR description/commentary and shipped artifacts (metadata, paths, CHANGELOG).
issues.detail: The PR text references compute_image_publicly_shared while the directory, CheckID, class, and CHANGELOG use compute_image_not_publicly_shared. The check name is the contract identifier callers and dashboards bind to. Pick one and propagate it everywhere before merge.

issues.description: Image ADT stores a precomputed boolean rather than the underlying IAM bindings/members.
issues.detail: The Image model carries publicly_shared: bool, discarding which role(s) and members granted public access. Storing the raw public principals (or bindings) keeps the abstraction self-describing, supports remediation/audit, and lets future checks reuse the data without service edits.

issues.description: Service test pins the leaky 'permission denied -> publicly_shared=False' behavior instead of the intended contract.
issues.detail: compute_service_test.py asserts images[2] (permission-denied case) has publicly_shared=False, conflating 'truly not shared' with 'policy fetch failed'. No check-level test exercises what the check reports when IAM is unreadable — the most security-relevant failure mode. Tests should assert intent, not leakage.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` in _get_images swallows all errors, conflating API failures with programmer faults.
issues.detail: Both try blocks catch Exception without narrowing. A malformed response missing a key would be logged as if it were an API permission error and the loop would continue with corrupted state. Narrow exception handling to anticipated API errors and let unexpected exceptions propagate or be surfaced distinctly.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a small, idiomatic check with two substantive contract problems. First, an IAM-policy fetch failure is silently coerced into publicly_shared=False, so PASS no longer means 'verified non-public' — all three reviewers flag this as the central correctness/abstraction defect. Second, the check name drifts between the PR description and the shipped artifacts (paths, metadata, CHANGELOG), which is the contract identifier callers bind to. Secondary concerns: the Image ADT bakes a verdict instead of carrying bindings, tests pin the leaky behavior rather than the intended postcondition, and exception handling is too broad. No reviewer found a hard correctness blocker beyond the unknown-policy issue.
